findings.summary: The increment is an unlocked read-modify-write, so two processes running at the same time can read the same value and one update is lost. Because `>` empties the file before writing, a reader that runs in that gap sees an empty file and resets the count to 1.

The file's contents go into arithmetic unchecked, so bash evaluates them as an expression. Non-numeric content silently resets the count, and content like `a[$(cmd)]` runs a command if anyone else can write the file.
